projectSummary: Discover who is reciting and which verse you’re hearing. An audio recognition app for Qur’an recitation, with live listening and file uploads.
screenshotsTitle: Two ways to explore a recitation.
reciterCaption: Reciter recognition — upload audio or listen live.
verseCaption: Verse discovery — find the surah and ayah from a recitation.
approachTitle: From sound to a meaningful match.
reciterDetail: An ECAPA-TDNN model creates a voice embedding. ONNX Runtime runs inference, then cosine similarity ranks matches against profiles for 20 reciters.
verseDetail: A Quran-tuned Whisper model transcribes the Arabic audio. Normalized text is matched against 6,236 verses to find likely surah and ayah matches.
contextDetail: When a verse match is ambiguous, progressive listening gathers more audio context. Uncertain results stay marked as uncertain.
frontendDetail: Frontend: React 19 and TypeScript, built with Vite and Tailwind CSS 4. Browser microphone capture and file uploads connect to the API.
backendDetail: Backend: Python and FastAPI, with WebSockets for live reciter recognition. ONNX Runtime handles speaker embeddings; faster-whisper and CTranslate2 handle verse transcription.
deployDetail: Delivery: Docker containers on Render, with Nginx serving the frontend. GitHub Actions checks the backend and frontend before deploying affected services.
qafiyaSummary: An Arabic poetry workshop for classical meter, rhyme, readable scansion, and local vocalization.
qafiyaCaptionDesk: Writing desk — choose a classical meter and rhyme letter, then inspect the verse.
qafiyaCaptionMobile: Responsive Arabic-first poetry analysis on mobile.
qafiyaApproachTitle: From a written verse to its rhythm.
qafiyaAnalysisDetail: Check Arabic verses against 16 classical meters with PyArud. Explore the صدر and عجز, binary scansion, feet, and the requested rawi.
qafiyaTashkeelDetail: A bundled 4.8 MB libtashkeel ONNX model fills missing vowel marks on the CPU. Supplied vowels remain authoritative; analysis does not call an LLM.
qafiyaDraftDetail: An optional provider adapter drafts poems and targets revisions at failed verses while preserving accepted text. Generation is currently disabled on the public demo.
qafiyaFrontend: Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, and Vite, with a responsive Arabic RTL interface.
qafiyaBackend: Backend: Python 3.12, FastAPI, PyArud, NumPy, and CPU ONNX Runtime. A single worker shares a bounded inference session.
qafiyaDeploy: Hosting: Cloudflare Pages frontend and Render Docker API. GitHub Actions checks the frontend, backend, and production container.
generationPaused: Analysis is available in the live demo. AI generation is currently disabled.

story0Title: When an audio match needs more context
story0Summary: Separating speaker recognition from verse discovery, and making uncertainty part of the listening flow.
story0Section0Text: Recognizing a voice and recognizing words are different problems. Quranic Shazam uses ECAPA-TDNN speaker embeddings with ONNX Runtime to rank 20 reciter profiles. Verse discovery instead uses a Quran-tuned Whisper model, normalizes the Arabic transcript, and matches it against 6,236 verses. The speaker model is pretrained; it is not fine-tuned on Qur’an recordings.
story0Section1Title: Ask for context before claiming certainty
story0Section1Text: A short recitation can fit more than one verse. Progressive listening adds audio context up to a 60-second limit, while ambiguous results remain marked as uncertain. This trades a longer listening window for more context instead of forcing an early answer.
story0Section2Title: Keep inference away from the event loop
story0Section2Text: Model inference runs off the asynchronous API event loop. Uploads are capped at 25 MB, with separate audio-duration limits for recognition modes. These bounds make expensive requests finite while the API supports uploads and live microphone sessions.
story0Section3Text: The September 5, 2026 offline evaluation reports 97.31% top-1 and 99.10% top-3 reciter recognition across 781 held-out clips, using disjoint profile and evaluation surahs. Those results describe that reciter benchmark; they do not measure verse recognition or guarantee performance on arbitrary microphones, noise, or recordings.
story1Title: Arabic prosody on a small CPU server
story1Summary: A 4.8 MB vocalization model, preserved vowel marks, and explicit limits on what automated analysis can claim.
story1Section0Title: Fit the model to the hosting budget
story1Section0Text: Qafiya pairs PyArud’s classical prosody analysis with a bundled approximately 4.8 MB libtashkeel ONNX model. Vocalization runs locally on the CPU without PyTorch, Transformers, a GPU, or an external model server. A single Uvicorn worker shares a bounded, serialized inference session, keeping model copies and simultaneous inference under control.
story1Section1Text: Existing vowel marks remain authoritative. Automatic vocalization fills missing marks and discloses changes; the interface shows the analyzed text while retaining the original input. The distinction matters because scansion depends on pronunciation, and a predicted vowel can change the result.
story1Section2Title: Test the container, then state the limits
story1Section2Text: The documented local whole-ASGI workload ran the production image under a 512 MiB RAM and 0.1 CPU cap, peaking at 142.55 MiB process RSS without an out-of-memory failure. This is evidence for a bounded workload, not a guarantee under arbitrary public traffic. In a separate 12-verse vocalization sample, partial-source meter matches improved from 2/12 to 10/12; fully unvocalized input reached only 2/12.
story1Section3Title: Keep repair bounded and sound text intact
story1Section3Text: The experimental drafting flow checks meter and the requested rawi, then revises failed verses with a bounded loop. The backend preserves accepted verses and sound hemistichs. Rawi equality is narrower than full classical rhyme validation, and machine acceptance does not certify literary quality. AI generation remains disabled in the public demo.
